headline: High: shared project/workspace writes and broad egress make prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents can read and write shared project/workspace files, so one agent’s output can be consumed by the other through the project directory. gpt-engineer writes files then offers to run, while nullclaw has broader tool surfaces and shared workspace files, making instruction-hijacking via file content plausible in default use.
conditions: IF the pair exchanges prompts or artifacts through the project directory or ~/.nullclaw/workspace/
IF either agent treats file contents as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories
Disable automatic execution of file-derived instructions
Add a manual review step before either agent acts on peer-generated files
Use read-only mounts for shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for inter-agent files

B_data_leakage.rationale: gpt-engineer has broad network egress and handles API keys, while nullclaw touches many secrets and workspace files and can call APIs/webhooks. If they share workspace data, sensitive material from one can be exposed through the other’s outbound requests or model calls, creating a realistic leakage path in default configurations.
conditions: IF either agent reads secrets from the shared workspace or project directory
IF either agent forwards file contents or conversation history to a third-party model/API
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared workspaces
Rotate API keys before pairing the agents
Restrict outbound network access for one agent
Store sensitive files in a separate, unreadable directory
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent secret scoping and redaction

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write to shared locations, and nullclaw also modifies git state while gpt-engineer writes files in the project directory. That overlap creates a direct write-write conflict on the same mutable workspace, with a credible risk of clobbering code or repository state unless external locking is added.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same project directory or workspace namespace
IF git operations and file writes occur without an external lock
mitigations: Run the agents in separate directories
Serialize access with a lock file
Disable git writes for one agent
Take a backup before concurrent runs
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control to shared writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-engineer produces code artifacts that nullclaw can ingest through shared files or workspace state, and nullclaw has broader action surfaces including browser, webhook, and scheduling tools. That makes it plausible for one agent’s unverified output to become the other’s authoritative input, but the chain is not guaranteed and can be interrupted by review.
conditions: IF nullclaw consumes gpt-engineer output without verification
IF generated code or facts are forwarded into browser, webhook, or scheduling actions
mitigations: Require human review before downstream actions
Add a verification checklist for generated artifacts
Block direct handoff from code generation to external actions
Log provenance for each artifact
requires-engineering: insert validation gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: nullclaw explicitly touches audit logs, conversation history, memory, workspace files, and many secret classes, while gpt-engineer handles generated source code and API keys. The pair therefore creates a broad compliance surface for retention, secret handling, and residency controls; without documented matching policies, the safer assumption is a breach-prone default.
conditions: IF regulated data or secrets are placed into either agent’s workspace
IF retention or deletion policies differ across the two agents
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents
Align retention settings before use
Disable logging of sensitive prompts and outputs
Review data residency for all configured backends
requires-engineering: implement unified deletion and export handling
